quest.title: The Toy War: Heating Up
quest.description: You receive another missive from the workshop. It seems that all is not proceeding as planned...
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x40, Enigmatic Copper Mainspring x60, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x2

dialogues.speaker: Arbon
dialogues.text: Did you ask about the story?

dialogues.speaker: Alberre
dialogues.text: I'm counting on you.

dialogues.speaker: Arbon
dialogues.text: The feedback on the board doesn't look right. Shouldn't we be receiving naught but high praise? It wasn't like this before.

dialogues.speaker: Alberre
dialogues.text: Quite unexpected, yes — I suspect foul play!

dialogues.speaker: Arbon
dialogues.text: Fortunately, our boss has, in his wisdom, prepared a contingency plan!

dialogues.speaker: Alberre
dialogues.text: Well, of course he has. Why else do you think he's the boss?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Arbon, Alberre, is Livre in? He's got something for us, apparently.

dialogues.speaker: Arbon
dialogues.text: Ah, right on time. Here comes the contingency now!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What contingency?

dialogues.speaker: Arbon
dialogues.text: Well, that's you. That's what the boss said, but he's not here right now, so let us explain.

dialogues.speaker: Alberre
dialogues.text: Just a short explanation, once again.

dialogues.speaker: Arbon
dialogues.text: During the last two days, we released the results of our Champion Duelist Plan to the public.

dialogues.speaker: Arbon
dialogues.text: We've also started pre-orders that will allow people to pay half the price as a deposit and thus qualify for early access.

dialogues.speaker: Arbon
dialogues.text: We also placed an evaluation column — that is to say, the message board at the door of our store — upon which people could leave their profuse praises.

dialogues.speaker: Alberre
dialogues.text: This is what they call "building hype."

dialogues.speaker: Arbon
dialogues.text: Just as the boss expected, our store really did get very popular — but very few people placed pre-orders, and the amount of praise left in the other column was also lamentably low.

dialogues.speaker: Alberre
dialogues.text: "You lack sincerity" this, "where's the internal quality control" that, "get with the times"... Such are the reviews we've gotten.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like the market wasn't quite what you expected, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Arbon
dialogues.text: I fear things are not so simple. We have a saying around here, that where there's smoke, there's fire — that is to say that something never arises from nothing!

dialogues.speaker: Arbon
dialogues.text: In other words, someone is spreading rumors!

dialogues.speaker: Alberre
dialogues.text: Baseless, scurrilous rumors that smear us!

dialogues.speaker: Arbon
dialogues.text: That smear us irresponsibly!

dialogues.speaker: Alberre
dialogues.text: That irresponsibly invent disparaging fictions and defamatory fabrications!

dialogues.speaker: Arbon
dialogues.text: The boss is sure that his brother is the only one who can be behind the smear campaign. Lepaute Horlogerie has the most to be worried about if this plan succeeds, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, what do you wanna do? Hire us to smear them right back?

dialogues.speaker: Arbon
dialogues.text: Lady Furina above! How could you ever think such a thing?

dialogues.speaker: Arbon
dialogues.text: Our boss is Caron's elder brother, after all! Even if they might stoop to such low and vulgar means, we will defeat them fair and square!

dialogues.speaker: Alberre
dialogues.text: Exactly! Only this way can the elder brother reform his wayward little brother.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What are we needed for, in that case?

dialogues.speaker: Arbon
dialogues.text: To get them to reveal what they mean by "sincerity" and "internal quality control," of course!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Reveal what now?

dialogues.speaker: Alberre
dialogues.text: Is that not fair? And is Fontaine not the nation of fairness?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's not what "fairness" means!

dialogues.speaker: Arbon
dialogues.text: The boss said that since everyone seems to think that the other party's packaging has been done with sincerity, we should keep pace with them.

dialogues.speaker: Arbon
dialogues.text: We shall package our Champion Duelists as they package adventurers. Adding that to our wealth of data will guarantee us a comeback victory!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Packaging? Nah, they just turned an adventurer's tale into a toy, that's all.

dialogues.speaker: Arbon
dialogues.text: Ohh, that must be it! Please, ask them what it is! That story must be the packaging we speak of.

dialogues.speaker: Alberre
dialogues.text: I, too, have heard a little something. It seems that while Caron was drunk, he accidentally let slip that this toy was made due to a certain person.

dialogues.speaker: Arbon
dialogues.text: Imagine what a grand tale they must've shared, to inspire such words from him!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Huh, really? Y'know, {NICKNAME}, Paimon's suddenly kinda curious as to what that story might be. Why don't we try going back and asking?

dialogues.speaker: Arbon
dialogues.text: #Will you? Oh, splendid, splendid! We shall leave this in your capable hands, then, Ms. Paimon, {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}.

talks.objective: Talk to Caron, the shop owner

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: Hello again, dear customers. How have you been? Have you tried out the adventurer toy, by the way?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey there, Caron. Actually, we've got some things we wanted to consult you about, and yeah, it's about the toy.

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: Ah, a happy coincidence, then. I enjoy those — like a fortuitous opportunity to nap, or just happening to have enough Mora to buy what you'd like to. Ask away.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'd like to hear the story behind this toy.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's right. We've heard that you based this toy on someone — that's gotta be the adventurer who's the star of this tale, right?

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: Haha, I see, so that's your question. Well, that adventurer did indeed leave a deep impression on me.

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: I met an adventurer in Springvale when I was about to leave Mondstadt. It appeared that he had messed up some sort of meal delivery commission.

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: Apparently, he had encountered several waves of monsters on the way there, and not only had he missed the timing, but the food had also been bumped about. Knowing a thing or two about cooking, I helped him make a new serving.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, that sure was nice of you!

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: Well, but that's not all. You might find it hard to imagine, but that one attempt at cooking resulted in all manner of accidents.

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: The firewood got wet... a big hole got gouged in the bottom of the pot, and while I was plating up, I was hit by some flying stones from out of nowhere... One of them even bounced onto my head. Now that one really hurt!

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: Well, the job did eventually get done, albeit with a complaint from the customer that they had cracked a tooth on a stone while eating.

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: Lady Furina above... Surely it wasn't the stone that hit us on the head?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Uh, was this adventurer's name...

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: Bennett? That was his name — wait, do you two know him as well? Interesting fellow, that one.

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: Later, he took me to all sorts of rarely-visited places in Mondstadt to show his thanks. It was a pretty rough journey, but the uncommonly beautiful sights made it worth the effort.

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: I would've taken him for a travel enthusiast had he not told me that he had discovered those places by losing his footing during adventures, or from getting lost.

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: On the day of my return to Fontaine, he came to say goodbye, and there I asked him if he considered his unlucky disposition bothersome.

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: He just gave me a thumbs-up and said: "The world is full of all sorts of people — and maybe I just happen to be the unluckiest."

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: "But thanks to that, I've also become the bravest person — and that's given me access to sights only I can see."

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: What a brilliant way of putting things. Walking the path of misfortune with a big smile on one's face — perhaps that's the spirit of a true adventurer.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's right, Bennett's the most adventurous adventurer for sure!

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: Hehe, if bad luck can be infectious, perhaps that adventuring spirit could be too — and with any luck, the latter can spread far further than the former.

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: Heh. I wonder, will this story give you enough material for your report?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um... How did you figure that one out this time?

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: Where there's smoke, there's fire. That's what we say in Fontaine.

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: If you really wanted to know about this story, you'd have asked the first time. But since you're only doing that now, I can only guess that my brother put you up to it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So you really did know! Y'know, Paimon doesn't get why Livre would have such a dim view of you. You're pretty smart, and you seem like a nice guy...

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: It's anger, I think. He's probably still mad at me for what he sees as a betrayal.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? Betrayal!?

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: Our family is well-known for our skills in making clockwork devices. I've always been good at making toys of that sort, and while my brother isn't quite as good, he's got a real knack for doing business.

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: Since we both loved toys, we agreed that when we grew up, we would set up the best toy store ever. But it was only when we grew up that we realized that someone had to succeed the family business — that is to say, this shop.

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: My brother had a big fight with our father over that, and he went to strike out on his own. I, on the other hand, was convinced to stay — and is that not a betrayal?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... Does that really count, though?

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: Well, it wasn't a show of adventurousness, that was for sure. I was afraid that if I failed to make a name for myself out there, I'd have to come crawling back to the family business... I just couldn't take that pressure.

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: I've always been like that. I'd be the first to cry when we encountered some hooligans on the streets, but my brother would have me get behind him with a "don't worry, watch me send them flying with my knuckle sandwich!"

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Your relationship seems kinda complicated...

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: Well, I suppose that's how things played out, eh?

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: In any case, I'll be here if you have any other questions. You're always welcome here in my store.

dialogues.speaker: Arbon
dialogues.text: Boss, our two guests have returned.

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: Quick as ever, I see. I suppose you gained much from your investigations?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh. Y'know, Livre, why do you always show up later?

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: Heh, well, I suppose I am remiss. I shall strive to come earlier next time. Anyway, about that toy...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You tell Livre about Bennett. He frowns.

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: A toy based on an adventurer named Bennett? I see...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And another thing. We didn't ask him, but Paimon thinks your brother didn't badmouth your shop. He doesn't look like the type.

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: Oh? How so?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: He seems to be sorry about something concerning you.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You pass Caron's words on. Livre's gaze passes through you to what seems to be a place in the indeterminate distance, like a Kamera adjusting its focus.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After a while, a dissatisfied noise struggles its way out of his chest.

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: Hmph...

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: If you ask me, I don't think that idiot would do something like that either...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, so what was this whole contingency thing about?

dialogues.speaker: Arbon
dialogues.text: The boss was just looking for an excuse, I suppose.

dialogues.speaker: Alberre
dialogues.text: More likely than not, I say.

dialogues.speaker: Arbon
dialogues.text: Well, he is a businessman. Businessmen have reputations to consider.

dialogues.speaker: Alberre
dialogues.text: And he's the big brother, is he not? A big brother's got a name to uphold, you know.

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: Say any more, or you'll eat my knuckle sandwich.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Haha, Livre's exactly what Caron said he'd be like.

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: Well, dear guests, I was just thinking that I should go pay that idiot a visit.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, are you gonna put your differences aside and go ask him for advice, then?

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: Of course not. But if he thinks he's betrayed me and feels bad about that, shouldn't I give him the opportunity to apologize to my face?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He did say that... But Paimon doesn't think that that's the sort of betrayal someone needs to apologize for...

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: Well, it's decided... Arbon, there's no need for any further pre-orders. Return all deposits as needed, and keep that evaluation board.

dialogues.speaker: Arbon
dialogues.text: What? Boss! So we're not executing the plan anymore? What about the data collection?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: There's still time to make adjustments.

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: No, the data collection continues. I have other plans for that. And you've got payments to collect, don't you? I always do honest business.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Suspiciously honest, in this case!

dialogues.speaker: Alberre
dialogues.text: Ah, the boss is the boss, even when he's being stubborn.

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: Hmph. I wouldn't call his attitude toward toys completely worthless.

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: I'll pay a visit to Lepaute Horlogerie once the next two days of data collection are complete. I'd like you two to come too, good customers.

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: I've got some other things to settle here in the shop, so if you'll excuse me.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Livre turns and walks into his store.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Livre's got such an odd temper... He's not really going to ask for an apology, is he?

dialogues.speaker: Arbon
dialogues.text: Well, would you look at that? Our third party has brought about an opportunity for change once again!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Third party?

dialogues.speaker: Arbon
dialogues.text: That's the two of you, of course. Thanks to you, the differences between the two shop owners may yet be resolved. That's what happened previously, too!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Previously?

dialogues.speaker: Arbon
dialogues.text: Aye! Have you noticed how this shop is separated from Lepaute Horlogerie by the Northland Bank?

dialogues.speaker: Arbon
dialogues.text: Boss originally wanted to set up shop next to Lepaute Horlogerie to compete with them directly.

dialogues.speaker: Alberre
dialogues.text: Now I doubt that they knew about the boss's history when they reserved that space, but in some way, they became a mediator in the conflict, didn't they?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's super interesting! The Fatui love to meddle in other people's business, but this sort of meddling's a first for sure!

dialogues.speaker: Arbon
dialogues.text: And that's the importance of third parties, just like how a double act still needs an audience.

dialogues.speaker: Alberre
dialogues.text: Well, what about solo acts? Would things work with just one actor and one audience?

dialogues.speaker: Arbon
dialogues.text: Wait, are you trying to betray me too? You'd better watch out for my knuckle sandwich, then!

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: Do you have any other questions?
